questions.q: What are the four factors of production? Explain each.
answer: The resources used to produce goods and services are called the factors of production, and there are four of them.

answer.text: In economics, land means all the natural resources used in production — soil, water, minerals, forests and air.
Labour is the human effort, both physical and mental, used in producing goods and services.
Capital is the man-made goods used to produce more goods, such as tools, machines, buildings and money invested in a business.
The entrepreneur organises the other three factors, takes the key decisions and bears the risk of the enterprise. All four factors must work together, since none can produce anything alone.

questions.q: What reward does each factor of production earn?
answer: Each factor of production earns a reward for the part it plays in producing goods and services.

answer.text: The owner of land receives rent for its use, and labour is paid wages or a salary for the human effort it provides.
Capital earns interest as the return on the money and goods invested, and the entrepreneur earns profit, which is what remains after the other three factors have been paid.

Profit is not guaranteed: because the entrepreneur bears the risk of the business, the result may be a profit or a loss. Improving the quality of these factors, such as more skilled labour and better technology, raises productivity and rewards.

questions.q: How do the factors of production combine to produce goods and services, and why is each essential?

answer.text: requires four factors working together — land, labour, capital and enterprise — and the absence of any one halts production.

list: Land supplies natural resources and space on which activity takes place
Labour provides the human physical and mental effort that transforms resources
Capital — tools, machines, buildings and money — makes labour more productive
Enterprise (the entrepreneur) organises the other three, takes risks and makes decisions

answer.text: do these factors turn raw resources into useful goods and services, which is why each is indispensable to the economy.

questions.q: Distinguish between physical capital and human capital, and explain why human capital is important.

answer.text: refers to the man-made goods used to produce other goods — tools, machines, buildings and raw materials.
refers to the stock of skill, knowledge, education and good health embodied in people.

list: Physical capital can be bought and sold in the market; human capital is built through education, training and healthcare
Machines are worked by people, so skilled and healthy workers make physical capital more productive
